Brian Babin

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 36, Harris County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative for Texas' 36th Congressional District (since 2015); dentist

Brian Babin is a Republican who has represented Texas' 36th Congressional District since January 2015 and chairs the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee. He defeated Jonathan Mitchell in the Republican primary on March 3, 2026. He faces Democrat Rhonda Hart in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Babin stands

Immigration / birthright citizenship
Authored the Birthright Citizenship Act and argues that Congress must act to reform birthright citizenship laws to restore what he calls the original intent of the Fourteenth Amendment.
Federal budget and taxes
Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in July 2025.
Space / NASA
Supports Texas's proposal to host the U.S. Space Academy and led a Texas delegation letter endorsing it.
Health care
Introduced the ORTHO Act (H.R. 9829) to set patient safety standards for orthodontic treatment delivered through teledentistry.
Transportation / infrastructure
Introduced the I-47 Future Interstate Act of 2026, which would designate U.S. Route 287 as Interstate 47.
Defense
Co-introduced a bipartisan bill to protect MQ-9 drone capabilities and keep Air National Guard readiness intact.
Government transparency / Epstein files
Voted to release the Epstein files and said he supports full transparency, while calling the effort a political sideshow.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas District 36, 2015–present
  • Chairman, House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology
  • Member, House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee; Co-Chair, Border Security Caucus
  • Dentist (more than 40 years of practice)
  • U.S. Air Force veteran
  • Education: Forest Park High School; Lamar University; University of Texas Dental Branch
